name: NJ-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Norcross holds an overwhelming financial edge ($2.4M on hand vs ~$2K for Galdo)
District leans Democratic by about ten points
Prediction markets price a Democratic hold around 96%

model.rationale: Norcross combines a ten-point Democratic district lean with a massive fundraising advantage — roughly $2.4 million on hand against about $2,000 for Galdo — and no reported outside spending against him. Markets price his re-election near certain, and nothing in the available evidence points to a competitive race.
model.watch: A late wave of outside money for Galdo or a sharply Republican national environment could narrow the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Donald Norcross, the Democratic incumbent in this South Jersey district, enters the general election with a substantial edge. The district carries a Democratic lean of about ten points, and Norcross has built a campaign fund of roughly $2.4 million, including $1.9 million raised this cycle. His Republican challenger, Damon Galdo, has raised about $16,000 and reported only around $2,000 on hand. No outside spending against the incumbent has been reported.

No public polls of the race are available, and national raters have not issued individual assessments, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and the money gap. Prediction markets give Democrats about a 96 percent chance of holding the seat. The expected winning margin sits near twenty points, consistent with the district's partisan tilt plus the advantages of incumbency and overwhelming financial superiority. Galdo would need a dramatic shift in conditions to make the race competitive.
